S1-01.title: A/R Summary opens with customers in name order, A to Z

fields.title: A/R Summary opens with customers in name order, A to Z
fields.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Four customers have open invoices on today's date: {Customer-A}, {Customer-B}, {Customer-C} and {Customer-D}. Their names start with the same word and then differ by a number, a dash or capitals, as in the example.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-01 10 Trucking, {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-01 2 Trucking, {Customer-C} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-01 A-1 Towing, {Customer-D} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-01 a1 towing.
  • Starting screen: A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Without clicking any column header, find the four customers in the list (use the page controls if they are on a later page).
  2. Read the order of the four customers from top to bottom.
  3. Look at the header of the customer name column (the first column).
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: all four customers are listed.
  • Step 2: they read {Customer-A}, then {Customer-B}, then {Customer-C}, then {Customer-D} (other customers may sit between them). With the example names: "10 Trucking" comes before "2 Trucking" because names compare character by character, and "A-1 Towing" comes before "a1 towing" because capitals are ignored and the dash compares as a character.
  • Step 3: the customer name column (the first column) is marked as the sorted column (a small arrow beside its heading).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order)

  • S1-R1: “A/R Summary opens with customers in name order, A to Z; A/P Summary opens with vendors in name order, A to Z.”
  • S1-R2: “Name order compares names ignoring capitals, in plain character order: digits and punctuation compare as characters, so "10 Trucking" comes before "2 Trucking" and "A-1 Towing" before "a1 towing".”
  • S1-R7: “The column the report opened on is marked as sorted: the name column on the Summaries and Detail reports, the Date column on Collection and Unpaid Invoices.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 1 "Opening order and header sorting" (board Main.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p1-a-r-aging-summary-opens-a-to-z.png: figure "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z" (This build (after)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting"
  • ar-ap-p7-a-r-summary-date-only.png: figure "A/R Aging Summary as it opens today" (Production (before)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting" (today's look, for comparison only)

The design's own words:

  • "Customer name order the way QuickBooks sorts ("10 Trucking" before "2 Trucking"), marked on the Customer header. S1-R1, S1-R2, S1-R4, S1-R7, S1-R8." (caption of "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z")
  • "Customers come back in no set order, and no column header can be clicked to sort." (caption of "A/R Aging Summary as it opens today")

S1-05.title: Two customer names that differ only in capitals keep one order everywhere

fields.title: Two customer names that differ only in capitals keep one order everywhere
fields.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two customers have open invoices on today's date and their names differ only in capitals: {Customer-A} and {Customer-B}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-05 Ace Towing and {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-05 ACE TOWING.
  • Starting screen: A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Find {Customer-A} and {Customer-B} in the list and note which one is higher.
  2. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu at the right of the title.
  3. Open the PDF and find the two names.
  4. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  5. Open the CSV in a spreadsheet program and find the two names.
  6. Reload the page and find the two names again.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the two customers sit next to each other (no other customer between them) in one order.
  • Step 2: the PDF downloads.
  • Step 3: the two names are in the same order as on screen.
  • Step 4: the CSV downloads.
  • Step 5: the two rows are in the same order as on screen.
  • Step 6: after the reload they are still in the same order.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV)

  • S1-R4: “Two names that compare equal are ordered by the plain lower-cased name, then by the customer or vendor itself, so the same two customers always come out in the same order on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV.”

Preconditions

fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the two customers sit next to each other (with accents ignored their names are the same).
  • Step 2: {Customer-A} (no accent) is above {Customer-B} (with the accent): the tie is broken by the lower-cased names as they are written, and a plain "e" comes before "é".

The PRD says names that compare equal are ordered "by the plain lower-cased name" but not how an accent counts; question 1 on Chris Ward's sheet (sent 22 Oct 2026) asks. The tech plan (21 Oct 2026) says it: the lower-cased names are compared as written, so "emile" comes before "émile". Nothing in the PRD contradicts it, so this case follows the tech plan (QA lead's ruling of 12 Aug 2026). If Chris answers differently, his answer wins and this case changes.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order)

From: Tech plan "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter — Technical Implementation Plan" (2026-10-21, uploaded 22 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

Expected results

    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S2-07 Alder, {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S2-07 Birch and {Customer-C} is ZZAUTOTEST S2-07 Cedar; {Document-A} and {Document-B} are invoices and {Document-C} is a credit memo.
  • Starting screen: A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu, with the "1-30 days past due" bucket expanded.

fields.custom_steps:

  7. Click the "Customer full name" header again.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: rows inside each aging bucket sort by Location, A to Z: in the "1-30 days past due" bucket the {Location-A} rows come before the {Location-B} row.
  • Step 2: Z to A: the {Location-B} row comes first.
  • Step 3: A to Z again, as in step 1. There is no unsorted state.
  • Step 4: rows inside each aging bucket sort by Transaction type, A to Z: read the Transaction type words top to bottom in the "1-30 days past due" bucket; they are in alphabetical order.
  • Step 5: Z to A: the same words in reverse alphabetical order.
  • Step 6: the report was already sorted by Customer full name, so this first click reverses it: in the "1-30 days past due" bucket, {Document-A} ({Customer-C}) first, then {Document-C} ({Customer-B}), then {Document-B} ({Customer-A}).
  • Step 7: A to Z again: {Document-B}, {Document-C}, {Document-A}.

S3-03.title: A/R Summary: the PDF and CSV match the rows and order on screen

fields.title: A/R Summary: the PDF and CSV match the rows and order on screen
fields.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The organization has open documents in these reports at two locations, {Location-A} and {Location-B}, and you are enrolled at both; {Location-A}'s name comes first in A to Z order.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
  • Customers {Customer-A} and {Customer-B} have open documents at both locations on today's date, at least two each, with different amounts.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S3-03 Export One and {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S3-03 Export Two.
  • Starting screen: A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu, with the Customer filter showing {Customer-A} and {Customer-B} ticked.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Click the "Total" header once.
  2. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu.
  3. Open the downloaded PDF and compare its rows with the screen, top to bottom.
  4. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  5. Open the CSV in a spreadsheet program and compare its rows with the screen.
  6. Without refreshing the page, click the the customer name column (the first column) header.
  7. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu again.
  8. Open the new CSV and compare its rows with the screen.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the rows sort by Total, largest first.
  • Step 2: the PDF downloads as a file and the "Success" message "Data exported successfully." shows.
  • Step 3: the PDF holds exactly the rows on screen for {Customer-A} and {Customer-B}, in the same order, and has a "Location" column, as the screen does (two locations are in view).
  • Step 4: the CSV downloads and the "Success" message "Data exported successfully." shows.
  • Step 5: the CSV holds exactly the same rows in the same order, with a "Location" column.
  • Step 6: the rows re-sort by name.
  • Step 7: the CSV downloads with the "Success" message.
  • Step 8: the new CSV follows the new on-screen order, by name, not the earlier Total order.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV), story SV-11536 (Story 6, Location column)

  • S3-R2: “The PDF downloads as a file.”
  • S3-R3: “The PDF and the CSV contain exactly the rows on screen for the chosen as-of date, customer or vendor and locations, in the on-screen sort, including a sort changed after an earlier export, without refreshing the page.”
  • S3-R6: “The Location column appears in the export under the same rule as on screen (Story 6).”
  • S3-R10: “A successful export shows the native "Success" message, "Data exported successfully." An export with no rows downloads nothing and shows the native warning "Empty export", "Export didn't yield any results".”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Export succeeds | "Success", "Data exported successfully." | Success toast, as on the other reports”
  • S6-R2: “The column is shown when two or more locations are ticked (All locations counts when the report's list has two or more) and hidden when one or none is ticked.”

fields.custom_steps:
1. Set the as-of date to 10/15/2026.
  2. In the Location filter, untick {Location-B}.
  3. In the Past due filter, tick "91+ days", then "31-60 days".
  4. In the Customer filter, tick {Customer-B}, then {Customer-A}.
  5. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu.

fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the date chip reads "As of: 10/15/2026".

  • Step 3: both ranges are ticked.
  • Step 4: both customers are ticked; the chip reads "Customer: 2 customers".
  • Step 5: the PDF downloads.
  • Step 6: the lines read "As of Oct 15, 2026", then "Locations: " and {Location-A}'s name, then "Past due: 31-60 days, 91+ days" (menu order, not the order ticked), then "Customers: " and {Customer-B}, {Customer-A} (the order ticked). The PDF has no Location column.
  • Step 7: the CSV downloads.
  • Step 8: the CSV reads "As of: Oct 15, 2026", then the same Locations, Past due and Customers lines, and has no Location column.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R4: “Each export states the as-of date the user picked: the PDF "As of Oct 15, 2026", the CSV "As of: Oct 15, 2026" (format: three-letter month, day, four-digit year).”
  • S3-R5: “Each export states the locations under the as-of line: "Locations: All locations" when every location is ticked, otherwise "Locations: " followed by the ticked locations' names. Under it, only when set: "Past due: " and the ticked ranges in menu order (for example "Past due: 31-60 days, 91+ days"), then, for one ticked customer or vendor, "Customer: " or "Vendor: " and the name, and for several, "Customers: " or "Vendors: " and the names in the order they were ticked.”
  • S3-R6: “The Location column appears in the export under the same rule as on screen (Story 6).”
  • S6-N1: “With one location chosen, the column is hidden on screen and in the export.”
  • S5-R13: “The customer chip (A/R) and vendor chip (A/P) and their open menus are the native ones: Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter (person icon), Vendor exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors"). The menu has a search box, an "All customers" or "All vendors" row, the native line "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow." (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Customer: All customers" or "Vendor: All vendors" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the name when one is (shortened with "..." when long), and "Customer: N customers" or "Vendor: N vendors" when N are. fields.custom_preconds:

fields.custom_steps:
1. Read {Customer-A}'s name on screen.

  4. Read {Customer-A}'s name cell.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the name shows as it was typed, starting with "=".

fields.title: A/R Detail: the top-left chevron collapses and expands every group
fields.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The report has open invoices, credit memos and deposits in at least three aging buckets on today's date.
  • Starting screen: A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu, with every group collapsed.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Click the chevron on one bucket row.
  2. Hover over the chevron button in the table's top-left header cell.
  3. Click that chevron button.
  4. Look at the column header under the button and at the sort mark.
  5. Hover over the chevron button again.
  6. Click it.
  7. Look at each bucket row's own chevron.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: that bucket expands and its own chevron turns from pointing right to pointing down.
  • Step 2: the button's chevron points down (a group is expanded) and a tooltip above the button reads "Collapse all".
  • Step 3: every group collapses.
  • Step 4: the column under the button was not sorted: the sort mark is still on the column the report opened on.
  • Step 5: the chevron now points right and the tooltip reads "Expand all".
  • Step 6: every group expands, and the column under the button is still not sorted.
  • Step 7: every bucket row's chevron points down (open).

This release does not change how the groups open, so they open as today; the starting screen asks for every group collapsed, collapsing any that are open.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11534 (Story 4, Collapse all, Expand all and pinned group rows)

  • S4-R1: “The table's top-left header cell holds one chevron button. While any group is expanded it points down, its tooltip (above the button) reads "Collapse all", and a click collapses every group. S4-09.title: A/R Detail: the group row stays pinned under the headings

fields.title: A/R Detail: the group row stays pinned under the headings
fields.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • On today's date the report has two buckets, {Bucket-A} and the next bucket below it, {Bucket-B}, each with more lines than fit on the screen.
    For example: {Bucket-A} is "31-60 days past due" and {Bucket-B} is "1-30 days past due".
  • Starting screen: A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu, with the groups of {Bucket-A} and {Bucket-B} expanded.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Scroll down slowly into {Bucket-A}'s rows.
  2. Look at the pinned row.
  3. Keep scrolling until {Bucket-B}'s row reaches the top.
  4. Keep scrolling into {Bucket-B}'s rows.
  5. Scroll back up slowly until you are inside {Bucket-A}'s rows again.
  6. Scroll down fast through {Bucket-A}'s and {Bucket-B}'s rows.
  7. Scroll fast back up through {Bucket-B}'s and {Bucket-A}'s rows.
  8. Make the browser window 1200 px wide.
  9. Scroll the table sideways to the right.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Bucket-A}'s row stays pinned just under the column headings while its rows scroll beneath it.
  • Step 2: it shows the bucket's chevron (pointing down) and its label: the bucket's name and count; it shows no amounts (the bucket's sums stay in its own subtotal row).
  • Step 3: {Bucket-B}'s row pushes {Bucket-A}'s row up and off and takes its place; only one group row is pinned at a time.
  • Step 4: {Bucket-B}'s row stays pinned.
  • Step 5: the change reverses: {Bucket-A}'s row comes back down into the pinned place.
  • Step 6: at speed too, each pinned row is pushed up and replaced cleanly: it never covers the column headings or the Totals row at the bottom, and two group rows never overlap.
  • Step 7: the same going back up: each pinned row is replaced cleanly, never covers the column headings or the Totals row, and two group rows never overlap.
  • Step 8: the table now scrolls sideways (narrower than 1440 px).
  • Step 9: each group row's label ({Bucket-A}'s label) stays visible at the left while the columns move.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11534 (Story 4, Collapse all, Expand all and pinned group rows), story SV-11538 (Story 8, Report descriptions and layout)

  • S4-R6: “While the user scrolls through an expanded group, that group's row (the bucket label, customer or vendor) stays pinned just under the column headings. Only one group row is held at a time: when the next group's row reaches it, the next row pushes it up and off and takes its place. Scrolling back reverses this.”
  • S4-R7: “When the table scrolls sideways, each group row's label stays visible at the left.”
  • S8-R3: “The headline column (Open Balance; Total on the Summaries) is pinned to the right edge and bold on the header, every row, every expanded row and the Totals row, as on Sales By Customer. At 1440 pixels wide every column of all six reports is visible without scrolling sideways: the customer or vendor name and Transaction type wrap long values onto a second line, Location wraps only on A/P Detail (nine columns), column headings never wrap, and money, date and number columns never wrap. Narrower than 1440 pixels, the table scrolls sideways under the pinned column.”

From: Tech plan "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter — Technical Implementation Plan" (2026-10-21, uploaded 22 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Tech plan §3 D21: “Pinned group row = scroll-driven overlay (ReportPinnedGroupRow + useReportPinnedGroup) showing the group row's chevron and full label — on A/R Collection including "Phone:" and "Credit term:" (S9-R1/R2) — but no money cells (the group's subtotals stay in its own row)”
  • Tech plan §7 Manual testing checklist: “3. Fling-scroll a long expanded group: pinned row pushes up without overlapping header or totals.”

fields.custom_steps:
1. Scroll down slowly into {Vendor-A}'s rows.
  2. Look at the pinned row.

  4. Keep scrolling into {Vendor-B}'s rows.
  5. Scroll back up slowly until you are inside {Vendor-A}'s rows again.
  6. Scroll down fast through {Vendor-A}'s and {Vendor-B}'s rows.

  • Step 3: {Vendor-B}'s row pushes {Vendor-A}'s row up and off and takes its place; only one group row is pinned at a time.
  • Step 4: {Vendor-B}'s row stays pinned.
  • Step 5: the change reverses: {Vendor-A}'s row comes back down into the pinned place.
  • Step 6: at speed too, each pinned row is pushed up and replaced cleanly: it never covers the column headings or the Totals row at the bottom, and two group rows never overlap.
  • Step 7: the same going back up: each pinned row is replaced cleanly, never covers the column headings or the Totals row, and two group rows never overlap.
  • Step 8: the table now scrolls sideways (narrower than 1440 px).
  • Step 9: each group row's label ({Vendor-A}'s label) stays visible at the left while the columns move.

fields.custom_steps:

fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: four chips, in this order: the date chip "As of: " and today's date (for example "As of: 10/15/2026"), the Customer chip, the Past due chip, the Location chip. The date chip says "As of", no longer "Date".
  • Step 2: "Customer: All customers" with a person icon and "Past due: Any" with an hourglass icon, both in the resting (grey) style.
  • Step 3: "Location: All locations" with the location pin icon.
  • Step 4: every label matches exactly, capitals and punctuation included.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R1: “Each report's filter row is the native report filter row of the newer reports (Inventory Value, Sales By Customer), in this order on all six reports: the date chip ("As of: 10/15/2026"), the customer chip on the A/R reports or the vendor chip on the A/P reports, the Past due chip, then the Location chip.”
  • S5-R13: “The customer chip (A/R) and vendor chip (A/P) and their open menus are the native ones: Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter (person icon), Vendor exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors"). The menu has a search box, an "All customers" or "All vendors" row, the native line "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow." (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Customer: All customers" or "Vendor: All vendors" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the name when one is (shortened with "..." when long), and "Customer: N customers" or "Vendor: N vendors" when N are. The ticked customers or vendors narrow every row, group, total, page, sort and export; the Location list does not change (S5-R3).”
  • S5-R15: “The Past due chip and its open menu are the same native checkbox dropdown as Customer and Location: label "Past due", an hourglass icon, an "Any" row, the native line "All ranges are included. Pick one or more to narrow." while none is ticked, then "1-30 days", "31-60 days", "61-90 days", "91+ days", in that order; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Past due: Any" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the range when one is (for example "Past due: 91+ days"), and "Past due: N ranges" when N are. Ticking all four reads "Past due: 4 ranges", not Any, because Any also keeps invoices and bills that are not due yet. The ranges are the reports' own aging buckets: 1 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 to 90 and more than 90 days past the due date on the as-of date.”
  • S5-R6: “The chip reads "Location: All locations" when every location is ticked, the location's name when one is ticked (shortened with "..." when long), "Location: N locations" when N are ticked, and "Location: No locations" when none is.”
  • S5-R2: “The Location chip and its open menu are the native ones, exactly as on Sales By Customer, Inventory Value and Work In Progress: label "Location" with the location pin icon; the menu shows a "Select all" row, a "{N} selected" count, the locations with the ticked ones first, a search box with the placeholder "Search locations" once there are more than 8 locations, and "Clear selection".”
  • S5-R10a: “Filter choices are not remembered between visits: opening a report from the Reports menu starts on today's as-of date, no customer or vendor, Past due Any, and All locations.”
  • What changes for existing users: “The date filter is labelled "As of" (was "Date"). On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices the Customer or Vendor chip now comes after it.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 7 "Filters and call list" (board Filters.dc.html).   • ar-ap-p7-past-due-menu.png: figure "Past due menu" (New in this build), board "7. Filters and call list"
  • ar-ap-p7-past-due-ticked.png: figure "Past due ticked" (New in this build), board "7. Filters and call list"
  • ar-ap-p7-a-r-summary-date-only.png: figure "A/R Summary: date only" (Production (before)), board "7. Filters and call list" (today's look, for comparison only)

The design's own words:

  • "As of, Customer (Vendor on A/P), Past due, Location. "Customer: All customers" and "Past due: Any" rest grey, Past due with the design system’s hourglass icon. S5-R1, S5-R13, S5-R15." (caption of "Four chips on every report")
  • "The native checkbox menu: "Any" ticked, "All ranges are included. Pick one or more to narrow.", then 1-30 days, 31-60 days, 61-90 days, 91+ days. S5-R15, S5-N3." (caption of "Past due menu")
  • "31-60 days and 91+ days ticked: the chip reads "Past due: 2 ranges" in blue. The Summary lists only customers with an amount in those ranges, at full balances; the Totals row adds up exactly these rows. S5-R15, S5-R16, S5-R17, S5-R18, S5-R19." (caption of "Past due ticked")
  • "The Summaries and Detail reports have no customer, vendor or past due filter today." (caption of "A/R Summary: date only")

Design note (DR-04): the design shows the Customer menu with two ticked shows the ticked names as tags in the search box, a clear "×", and "2 selected" on the "All customers" row. Closed without a question: No conflict: PRD S5-R13 "Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter"; the PRD lists the menu's main rows, the design shows the native extras. S5-35.title: A/R Collection: a link with an unknown customer ignores it

fields.title: A/R Collection: a link with an unknown customer ignores it
fields.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has overdue invoices on today's date.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S5-35 Old Link.
  • Starting screen: A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. In the Customer filter, tick {Customer-A}.
  2. Copy the page address.
  3. Paste the copied address into the address bar.
  4. In the address bar, after {Customer-A}'s code (the text after "customerIds="), add a comma and "Nobody".
  5. Press Enter.
  6. Read the Customer chip and the groups.
  7. Paste the copied address into the address bar again.
  8. In the address bar, replace everything after "customerIds=" with "Nobody".
  9. Press Enter.
  10. Read the Customer chip.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the chip reads "Customer: " and {Customer-A}'s name; only {Customer-A}'s group is listed.
  • Step 2: the address carries "customerIds=" followed by {Customer-A}'s code (a long code, not the name).
  • Step 3: the copied address shows in the address bar.
  • Step 4: the address bar shows {Customer-A}'s code, a comma and "Nobody" after "customerIds=".
  • Step 5: the report loads normally, with no error.
  • Step 6: the chip reads "Customer: " and {Customer-A}'s name and only {Customer-A}'s group is listed: the unknown customer is ignored.
  • Step 7: the copied address shows in the address bar.
  • Step 8: the address bar shows "Nobody" after "customerIds=".
  • Step 9: the report loads normally, with no error.
  • Step 10: "Customer: All customers" in the resting (grey) style: with no known customer left, the link opens as if none were ticked.

Why: a link saved earlier can name a customer that was since deleted or merged; the tech plan says such a link must still open the report.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R19: “removed the older single-threshold Past due link.”
  • S5-R14: “A customer or vendor ticked through a link, a reload or a Summary drill-down is named and ticked on the chip, even when it is not among the first results of the chip's search.”

From: Tech plan "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter — Technical Implementation Plan" (2026-10-21, uploaded 22 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Tech plan §3 D29: “Unknown or unresolvable customer/vendor/location ids in a link are dropped by the FE during the opening reconcile (resolve endpoint / option list) before any request, so the BE 422 is never reached from the UI”
  • Tech plan §3 D29, rationale: “Mirrors S5-N2 for customers/vendors (a deleted or merged customer in an old link must not break the report).”
  • Tech plan §3 D30: “URL keys asOfDate, customerIds / vendorIds, pastDue, locationIds (repeated keys written, comma lists also read); legacy customerId / vendorId read once as aliases.”

DATA-01.title: A/R Summary: 30 customers per page, none repeated or skipped

fields.title: A/R Summary: 30 customers per page, none repeated or skipped
fields.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Between 31 and 90 customers have open documents on today's date.
    For example: the QA organization's A/R Summary has 46 customers.
  • Starting screen: A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  2. Count the customers in the CSV (each name once).
  3. Count the customers on the first page and note the last one.
  4. Go to the next page (or scroll until the next ones load).
  5. Read every page to the end, writing down each customer's name.
  6. Click the "Total" header.
  7. Read every page again, writing down each name.
  8. In the Past due filter, tick "1-30 days" and "91+ days".
  9. Read every page again, writing down each name.
  10. Read the Totals row on each page.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the CSV downloads.
  • Step 2: note the number of customers (for example 46).
  • Step 3: exactly 30 customers.
  • Step 4: the next page starts with the customer that comes right after the last one of the first page, not a repeat.
  • Step 5: every customer appears exactly once and the count equals the CSV's.
  • Step 6: the rows sort by Total, largest first.
  • Step 7: in this sort too, every customer appears exactly once and none is missing.
  • Step 8: the report reloads with only those two ranges.
  • Step 9: every customer left by the filter appears exactly once; none repeats between pages.
  • Step 10: the Totals row reads the same on every page and adds up every row the filters leave, not only the rows on that page.

Whether the next 30 come by page buttons or by scrolling is question 5; story SV-11531 still says "Paging (30 rows per page)" for every report, PRD v5 is followed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S1-R8: “paging stated per report (30 customers or vendors per page on the Summaries, A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices; 100 lines per bucket, then scroll, on the Detail reports). S4-R4: the 100-lines-then-scroll rule now covers A/R Detail too.”
  • S5-R18: “The Totals row always adds up exactly the rows the filters leave (customer or vendor, Past due, Location), on screen on every page, in the PDF and in the CSV. On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices this fixes today's Totals row, which ignores the customer or vendor filter.”
  • What changes for existing users: “A/R reports no longer come out in an unpredictable order; A/R Summary and A/R Collection no longer repeat or skip customers between pages.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 1 "Opening order and header sorting" (board Main.dc.html); page 7 "Filters and call list" (board Filters.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p7-past-due-ticked.png: figure "Past due ticked" (New in this build), board "7. Filters and call list"
  • ar-ap-p1-a-r-aging-summary-opens-a-to-z.png: figure "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z" (This build (after)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting"
  • ar-ap-p7-call-list-on-a-r-collection.png: figure "Call list on A/R Collection" (New in this build), board "7. Filters and call list"
  • ar-ap-p7-a-r-summary-date-only.png: figure "A/R Aging Summary as it opens today" (Production (before)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting" (today's look, for comparison only)

The design's own words:

  • "31-60 days and 91+ days ticked: the chip reads "Past due: 2 ranges" in blue. The Summary lists only customers with an amount in those ranges, at full balances; the Totals row adds up exactly these rows. S5-R15, S5-R16, S5-R17, S5-R18, S5-R19." (caption of "Past due ticked")
  • "Customer name order the way QuickBooks sorts ("10 Trucking" before "2 Trucking"), marked on the Customer header. S1-R1, S1-R2, S1-R4, S1-R7, S1-R8." (caption of "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z")
  • "Customer picked: the group row shows "Phone:" and, for users with View and Manage AP/AR Data, "Credit term:". The Totals row follows the customer filter. S9-R1, S9-R2, S5-R18. Exports carry the same lines and columns: S9-R3, S3-R5, S3-R8a." (caption of "Call list on A/R Collection")
  • "Customers come back in no set order, and no column header can be clicked to sort." (caption of "A/R Aging Summary as it opens today")

Nothing else is open for the three on today's date.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST DATA-07 Alpha, {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST DATA-07 Bravo and {Customer-C} is ZZAUTOTEST DATA-07 Charlie.
  • Starting screen: A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.

  • Step 3: the report narrows to {Location-A}.
  • Step 4: {Customer-A}'s Total is $850.00 (1,000.00 − 150.00, its {Location-A} documents only); {Customer-B}'s is $700.00; the Totals row's Total is $1,550.00.

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location), story SV-11536 (Story 6, Location column)

  • S5-R18: “The Totals row always adds up exactly the rows the filters leave (customer or vendor, Past due, Location), on screen on every page, in the PDF and in the CSV. On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices this fixes today's Totals row, which ignores the customer or vendor filter.”
  • S5-R8: “On the Summaries, a customer's or vendor's row adds up only their open documents at the chosen locations; a customer or vendor with nothing open there is not listed.”
  • S5-R17: “With ranges ticked, A/R Summary and A/P Summary list only the customers or vendors with some open invoice or bill amount in a ticked range; their rows show their full balances in every bucket.”
  • S6-R4: “On A/R Summary and A/P Summary a row shows the location's name when all of that customer's or vendor's open documents at the chosen locations are at one location, otherwise "Multiple".”
  • Key Decisions, row location: “A row belongs to the location of its own open document (the invoice, credit memo or deposit; the bill or vendor credit), the same location the Location column shows. fields.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has eight open invoices on today's date: one not yet due, and one each 1, 30, 31, 60, 61, 90 and 91 days past its due date.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST DATA-16 Boundaries; the invoices are $10.00, $1.00, $30.00, $31.00, $60.00, $61.00, $90.00 and $91.00 in that order.
  • Starting screen: A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu, with only {Customer-A} ticked in the Customer filter and every group expanded.

fields.custom_steps:
1. In the Past due filter, tick "1-30 days" only.
  2. In the Past due filter, untick "1-30 days".
  3. Tick "31-60 days".
  4. Untick "31-60 days".
  5. Tick "61-90 days".
  6. Untick "61-90 days".
  7. Tick "91+ days".
  8. In the Past due filter, tick all four ranges.
  9. In the Past due filter, untick all four.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the Totals row reads $31.00: only the invoices 1 and 30 days past due remain (expand the groups to see them).
  • Step 2: "1-30 days" is unticked.
  • Step 3: $91.00: only the 31 and 60 day invoices.
  • Step 4: "31-60 days" is unticked.
  • Step 5: $151.00: only the 61 and 90 day invoices.
  • Step 6: "61-90 days" is unticked.
  • Step 7: $91.00: only the 91 day invoice.
  • Step 8: the chip reads "Past due: 4 ranges" and the invoice that is not yet due is gone (Totals $364.00).
  • Step 9: "Past due: Any" and all eight invoices show (Totals $374.00).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R15: “The Past due chip and its open menu are the same native checkbox dropdown as Customer and Location: label "Past due", an hourglass icon, an "Any" row, the native line "All ranges are included. Pick one or more to narrow." while none is ticked, then "1-30 days", "31-60 days", "61-90 days", "91+ days", in that order; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Past due: Any" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the range when one is (for example "Past due: 91+ days"), and "Past due: N ranges" when N are. fields.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The organization has open documents in these reports at two locations, {Location-A} and {Location-B}, and you are enrolled at both; {Location-A}'s name comes first in A to Z order.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has open invoices only at {Location-B}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST D-19 States.
  • You can switch this computer's network connection off and on (for example Wi-Fi).
  • Starting screen: A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.
  • Sales By Customer (Reports, then "Sales By Customer" under PERFORMANCE in the left menu) is open in a second tab of the same window, for comparison.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Change the as-of date to yesterday and watch the table straight away.
  2. Change the as-of date back to today.
  3. In the Location menu, untick {Location-B}.
  4. In the Customer filter, tick {Customer-A}.
  5. Read the empty state, letter for letter, and compare it with Sales By Customer's empty state.
  6. Click "Clear all filters".
  7. Switch the network connection off.
  8. Change the as-of date to yesterday.
  9. Read the table area and the message.
  10. Switch the network back on.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the native table progress bar shows while the report loads.
  • Step 2: the report shows today again.
  • Step 3: the report narrows to {Location-A}.
  • Step 4: the report has no rows: {Customer-A} has nothing open at {Location-A}.
  • Step 5: "No record matches these filters" and "Try changing filters to widen your results.", with a "Clear all filters" button, in the native empty-state look of Sales By Customer; no Totals row.
  • Step 6: the filters return to their defaults and rows show.
  • Step 7: the computer is offline.
  • Step 8: the report fails to load.
  • Step 9: "Something went wrong loading this report. Please try again." in place of the rows, and the standard error message as well.
  • Step 10: the connection is back.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11538 (Story 8, Report descriptions and layout)

  • S8-R5: “While a report loads it shows the native table progress bar. When the filters leave no rows, it shows the native empty state: "No record matches these filters" and "Try changing filters to widen your results.", with a "Clear all filters" button when a customer or vendor, Past due or Location is chosen; that button keeps the as-of date and returns the customer or vendor, Past due and Location to their defaults (every location ticked).”
  • S8-R6: “If a report fails to load, it shows "Something went wrong loading this report. Please try again." in place of the rows, with the standard error message.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Filters leave no rows | "No record matches these filters", "Try changing filters to widen your results." | Native empty state with "Clear all filters"”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Report fails to load | "Something went wrong loading this report. Please try again." | In place of the rows, plus the standard error toast”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 4 "Location filter and Location column" (board Location.dc.html). The design pictures one empty state (No locations on A/R Detail); the loading bar and the load error are not drawn.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p4-cleared-no-locations.png: figure "Cleared: No locations" (This build (after)), board "4. Location filter and Location column"

The design's own words:

  • ""Clear selection" leaves no location chosen: the chip reads "Location: No locations" and stays visible, and the table shows the native empty state "No record matches these filters" with "Clear all filters". S5-R6a, S5-R9." (caption of "Cleared: No locations")

Difference from the PRD (DD-03): the PRD says with no location ticked, "the native empty state (S8-R5) with "Clear all filters", no totals and no Location column" (S5-R6a); the design shows "Location: No locations" with a Totals row reading $0.00 and $0.00 under the headings, above the empty state. This case follows the PRD; the difference is question 13 on Chris Ward's question sheet (added 22 Oct 2026); the design version is held in D-78.

fields.custom_preconds:

fields.custom_steps:
1. Look at the table's top-left header cell.
  2. Look at each bucket row's own chevron.

  8. Hover over the top-left chevron button.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: one chevron button, the design system's chevron icon, in the top-left header cell, pointing right (every group collapsed).
  • Step 2: every bucket row shows the same chevron, pointing right when closed.
  • Step 3: a tooltip above the button reads "Expand all", letter for letter.
  • Step 4: every bucket opens and its chevron points down.
  • Step 5: the tooltip above the button reads "Collapse all".
  • Step 6: the bucket's row stays pinned just under the column headings, with its label visible at the left.
  • Step 7: the page switches to dark theme; the pinned row is readable.
  • Step 8: the tooltip sits above the button and is readable in dark theme.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11534 (Story 4, Collapse all, Expand all and pinned group rows)

  • S4-R1: “The table's top-left header cell holds one chevron button. While any group is expanded it points down, its tooltip (above the button) reads "Collapse all", and a click collapses every group. When every group is collapsed it points right, its tooltip reads "Expand all", and a click expands every group.”
  • S4-R5: “Each group's own expand toggle uses the same chevron: pointing down when open, right when closed. Behavior is unchanged.”
  • S4-R6: “While the user scrolls through an expanded group, that group's row (the bucket label, customer or vendor) stays pinned just under the column headings. Only one group row is held at a time: when the next group's row reaches it, the next row pushes it up and off and takes its place. Scrolling back reverses this.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Collapse all / Expand all button | "Collapse all" / "Expand all" | Tooltip above the button”
  • Key Decisions, reuse rule: “The reuse rule. Every control on these reports reuses an existing ShopView pattern: the native filter chips, the native totals row and pinned headline column of the newer reports, the existing location-switch prompt, the design system's chevron icon. Nothing new is drawn. Basis: d-reuse-existing-pattern.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

  • ar-ap-p7-a-r-collection-date-and-customer-only.png: figure "A/R Collection, groups opened one by one" (Production (before)), board "3. Collapse all, Expand all and pinned group rows" (today's look, for comparison only)

(or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked.
